justification: Locations are written very frequently and read by driver ID, with no complex querying needed, so fast key lookups win.
Each profile is a self-contained unit with nested fields such as addresses, preferences and payment methods.
History is append-only and queried by rider ID and date range, which suits partition and clustering keys. A document database is an acceptable alternative.
Efficient traversal of connections, referral networks and fraud patterns needs relationships as first-class data.
Millions of posts per day need very high write throughput, and access follows a time-series pattern.
Counters and trending-topic caches need in-memory speed, backed by a column-family store for durable storage.
